state.issue:
jq: any_subexpr skips destructuring computed keys, so `. as {(input): $x}` fails at runtime

**Severity: Medium** — a valid program fails at runtime (exit 5) where jq succeeds; not a wording difference.

## Summary

`walk::any_subexpr` does not descend into a destructuring pattern's **computed object keys**, so
every one of its callers answers "no" for anything written in one. The visible case: `input` used
only inside a key makes `succinctly jq` fail outright.

Its own comment says why it skips them, and that reason is stale:

> `patterns` holds only destructuring names, never an `Expr`, so `Reduce`/`Foreach`/`AsPattern`
> need no descent into them.

Since #2734 a pattern can hold an `Expr` — `{(expr): $x}` keys are `ObjectKey::Expr`.

## Repro

Confirmed live against jq 1.7.1 and `succinctly` at `69a76d346` (`main`). Input is two documents,
`{"a":1}` then `"a"`:

```console
$ printf '{"a":1}\n"a"\n' | jq -c '. as {(input): $x} | $x'
1
$ printf '{"a":1}\n"a"\n' | succinctly jq -c '. as {(input): $x} | $x'
jq: error (at <stdin>:1): break
jq: error (at <stdin>:2): break                                   # exit 5
```

| filter | jq 1.7.1 | succinctly |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `. as {(input): $x} \| $x` | `1`, exit 0 | two `break` errors, exit 5 |
| `. as {(input\|tostring): $x} \| $x` | `1`, exit 0 | two `break` errors, exit 5 |
| `. as {("a"): $x} \| [$x, input]` *(control: `input` outside the key)* | `[1,"a"]` | `[1,"a"]` |

## Root cause

`src/jq/walk.rs`, `any_subexpr` — the `AsPattern`/`Reduce`/`Foreach` arms walk `expr`/`body`/
`input`/`init`/`update` but never `patterns`. The repro reaches it through `uses_input_builtins`,
which then reports that the program never calls `input`, so the input machinery is not set up.

That is one caller of roughly a dozen (`jq_runner.rs`, `yq_runner.rs`, many in `eval.rs`), and each
is a predicate over "does this tree contain X", so each can silently miss X in a key. Worth auditing
them all rather than fixing only `uses_input_builtins`.

## Why this is separate from #2971

#2971 (PR #3014) hit the same blind spot from `resolve.rs`: its re-keying walk was built on
`any_subexpr` and missed defs in computed keys. That PR worked around it *locally* — its own walk
descends pattern keys explicitly — and deliberately did not change `any_subexpr`, whose callers are
unrelated to reachability and deserve their own verification. This is the general fix.

#2957 (closed) is the same class in a different walker: `rewrite_namespaced_calls` skipped computed
destructuring keys.

## Suggested fix direction

Descend `patterns` in `any_subexpr` (via `ObjectKey::Expr`, recursing through `Pattern::Object`
entries and `Pattern::Array`), and correct the stale comment. #3014 has a small read-only pattern
walk that mirrors `check_pattern_keys`, which may be reusable. Then re-verify each caller — the
`input` row above is the one confirmed so far, not necessarily the only one.

Found while working #2971 (PR #3014).
